TriNet Zenefits pricing in 2026

The Zenefits brand has been fully absorbed into TriNet HR Platform. The three tiers (Essentials, Growth, Zen) remain. Pricing is quote-only with buying-committee bands at $8-$33 PEPM. TriNet PEO is sold alongside as a separate, benefits-aggregating product. Self-serve checkout was removed in the 2025 brand consolidation.

What the buying committee actually pays

Now sold alongside TriNet PEO. The PEO sells benefits arbitrage; the HR Platform sells software. The ledger applies a default 12% annual renewal uplift unless the buyer caps it in the MSA - our own central modelling assumption, adjustable on the renewal-uplift page, not a vendor-published rate.

What does the platform cost in 2026?

Essentials ~$8 PEPM, Growth ~$17 PEPM, Zen ~$33 PEPM (all buying-committee bands; TriNet publishes a quote form not list rates).

How do the tiers map to old Zenefits pricing?

Essentials maps directly. Growth replaces the old Growth tier with added Performance and Compensation. Zen bundles dedicated CSM, advanced analytics, and compliance support.

TriNet PEO vs TriNet HR Platform on cost?

PEO sells benefits aggregation (master health plan, workers comp pass-through) for $110-$180 PEPM admin fee. HR Platform sells software only at $8-$33 PEPM.

What is bundled vs add-on?

Payroll, Benefits Administration, and Compliance are bundled at all tiers. Performance, Compensation, and dedicated CSM step up by tier.

When does TriNet beat Justworks or Insperity?

For sub-50-employee SMBs that want software-style pricing rather than PEO admin fees. Justworks wins on simplicity; Insperity wins on full-service HR support; TriNet HR Platform wins on software UX.
